bluf: InfoTrust is a US analytics consultancy and technology company selling data governance, marketing measurement and privacy tech to multi brand enterprises, and it sells no media. It leads with Google stack depth (one of only 32 Google Cloud Partners globally with its certification, per its about page), the Tag Inspector platform and productised packages. The Horus read is Tailwind at 61.6, best placed for measurement getting worse before it gets better. A rival should know price is not the wedge (Monsoon Doldrums, displacement 31.9): the openings are the absent AI visibility layer and a thin, old evidence book behind a 50+ Fortune 500 claim.
doing:
The positioning line, an analytics consultancy and technology company specialising in data governance, marketing measurement and privacy tech for multi brand enterprises, selling no media, decodes to a pure measurement house: it implements and governs the Google stack, audits tags and sells packages, not campaigns. The headline claim pairs 50+ Fortune 500 clients with a Nespresso GMP migration credited with 26% revenue growth. The partner list is the evidence: Google Marketing Platform Certified Sales Partner (SA360, DV360, CM360, GA360), Google Cloud Partner, a Google Tag Manager and Looker Studio support partner, a BigQuery and Vertex AI specialist, Amplitude, Osano, RudderStack.

The capability read is narrow: Data & Measurement scores 3 as the lead and only core line (analytics, data governance and privacy in the title and H1; Tag Inspector; the Nespresso case), three lines score 1 with no evidence note, breadth 4. The services list is a package ladder: data privacy, strategy and governance; data insights and activation; implementation and integration; Google Cloud services; the packages Insights, Implement, Integrity, Impact and Ignite; and Tag Inspector.

AI posture: data foundations, the Vertex AI marketing analytics specialism, predictive modeling in the Ignite package and an AI for marketing article series; no AI search or AI visibility line, and P1 is absent.

Moves: one undated rebrand, Tag Inspector folded into InfoTrust for a single brand; no news and no jobs are listed. Dated case pages are old: a 27 December 2016 batch (Beckfield College, Mumzworld, EasyClosets, Cowan’s Auctions), a 27 December 2018 batch, Lenovo and Gaia in 2019, then nothing until a medical device brand on 27 June 2025 and Nespresso on 6 March 2026. Resources dated 9 to 22 September 2026 carry Tag Inspector release notes.

Pricing: productised packages (Insights plans, Impact packages), prices not captured; P5 is making. Conspicuously absent: a founding year, an employee count, an HQ city or office, and any measurement of AI answers.
clients:
Client type: enterprise and multi brand, across retail and ecommerce, CPG, media and publishing, finance, insurance and crypto, and health and fitness; home market the US, no city or office listed.

The needs read lists 9 client rows, all case studies: 4 observed and 5 names only. Data and measurement sits on 4 rows, Web build on 2, Commerce on 1. Observed signals: Nespresso, data plus web plus commerce, dated 6 March 2026, a global GA4 migration credited with 26% revenue growth; Gaia, web plus data, a Google Analytics 360 implementation dated 22 October 2019 for a single page app; Ecentria, data, dated 4 June 2019, integrating analytics; Lenovo, data, dated 28 May 2019, tag governance with Tag Inspector. The 5 names only rows are FxPro, Beckfield College, Mumzworld, EasyClosets and the Cowan auctions page, the last four dated 27 December 2016 with page builder markup for excerpts: needs inferred from the sold mix.

The record holds work the rows do not: IQVIA on Tag Inspector (28 June 2019), Ramsey Solutions automating data accuracy with Tag Inspector, a global medical device brand on InfoTrust Insights (27 June 2025), a fitness client with franchise groups (23 October 2019), and a slug dated 22 September 2026 on a global fitness franchise cutting 800 hours of manual work. None of the 9 is shared with another tracked agency. The gap between 50+ Fortune 500 clients claimed and 9 rows on record is the question to ask.

Next: under KJ9 (Measurement gets worse before it gets better) it is very likely these enterprises buy more governance, consent and migration work, which it sells; under KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) it is likely, moderate confidence, that they also ask for AI answer measurement, which nothing in the record offers.

openings:
The computed openings are thin, one judgment (KJ5 exposure through Programmatic & CTV): the read favours it. The strongest opening is the AI layer: P1 is absent, AI Search / GEO scores 0, and nothing in the record measures citations or AI answers, so it is likely, moderate confidence, that a measurement specialist selling AI visibility as an audited product takes the next measurement budget from these enterprises. Falsifier: an AI answer or citation measurement package appearing in its record.

Second, the evidence book: 5 of its 9 clients are names only, four dated 27 December 2016, and only Nespresso (6 March 2026) and a medical device brand (27 June 2025) are recent, so dated enterprise proof is two cases deep; roughly even chance the 50+ Fortune 500 claim carries the room anyway. Third, onetrust on its own site beside an Osano partnership is a say/do question for the sales room. Price is not an opening: Doldrums at 36.9 and displacement 31.9 mean the book does not buy on price, and an offshore rival is unlikely to undercut productised packages. Hard to beat: Google partner depth and Tag Inspector; almost no chance a media agency out measures it inside GMP.
